reviews.text: When my dog ​​had a sudden seizure, I received a very kind and helpful response over the phone, even though it was outside of regular hours. It was difficult for me to visit in person due to the distance, but they reassured me with their words. I forgot to ask for the doctor's name, but I am filled with gratitude. Thank you so much.

I'm a patient of a senior 13-year-old cat at this clinic.

My cat is very timid and struggles quite a bit, so some vets said anesthesia was necessary even for checkups. However, when I visited Anihos, they gave me a very reassuring response, saying, "Just because she struggles a little...?" That convinced me to continue going there. (They were able to perform the checkup without anesthesia.)

I'm quite anxious and ask a lot of questions, but they answer them all thoroughly. They also perform full blood tests and provide advice.

Furthermore, when I have concerns, they provide samples of foods that might help, and I've found a therapeutic diet that suits my cat's condition.

However, since there isn't a designated vet, I see a different one each time, and I feel there are slight differences in their approaches to diet and treatment.

Regarding the health checkup results, I was told over the phone that we should do checkups every six months, but when I went back six months later, the vet said, "The chart says you need another checkup in two months, but it's been a while..."

All of these were different vets.

This wasn't a clear-cut illness (the numbers were just within the normal range), and the results suggested that we could monitor it. However, even as a layperson, I've found various opinions, and I understand that different doctors have different views.
In fact, the next results weren't serious either, and we were told that checkups every six months would be sufficient.

Regarding diet, some doctors preferred dry food only, while others insisted on continuing with a 50/50 mix. The former advice came before the health checkup results, so perhaps the doctor who saw the good results suggested continuing as is.

Since my dog ​​is quite unruly, brushing his teeth is difficult, and I understand why they suggested dry food only to prevent tartar buildup.

Overall, I get the impression that not having a regular vet can lead to confusion, and some people might not get along with a doctor who can't think objectively.

Therefore, I think it might be a good idea to choose a few doctors who are a good fit, in case my dog ​​develops an illness requiring ongoing treatment as he gets older.

Thank you for your continued support.

Thank you as always.

I had been taking my cat to the vet for urinary tract stones. The symptoms had worsened, so I took him earlier than scheduled, but the vet insisted everything was fine. I pressed him, pointing out that the vomiting and aggressive behavior during urination were clearly abnormal. He finally had an ultrasound and, confirming there was no urine in his bladder, he was fine and was given IV fluids and painkillers. I felt uncomfortable with the IV and asked why, and he gave me a plausible explanation, so I let him.

After returning home, his condition continued to worsen. Initially, there was a lump between his legs, and when I called, they explained it was due to the IV drip leaking down. I did think that might be the case, but then he started having blood in his urine. I called again, and they said it was normal because of the urinary tract stones. However, he was only urinating in small amounts, and he was constantly urinating while walking around the house. When I explained this, they said, "He's urinating while walking, so if that's all he's producing, it's fine!" But how can it be okay when he's urinating blood in his urine?

While I was staying up all night caring for my cat, he had a small seizure. I tried calling several times, but couldn't get through.

I thought she might have been cold because she had been sleeping warmly, but a few hours later, she suddenly jumped out of her house, thrashed around, and had seizures. When I called again, the same doctor who had answered the previous calls answered with a sleepy voice. It seemed he was the on-call doctor.

He said he hadn't been able to answer the phone because he was in surgery. He also said that there was nothing they could do if I came now, and that I should bring her in again if she had another seizure. ...

I hung up and started looking for another hospital, when she immediately had another seizure. This time it was even more violent, she jumped and bounced around like a poltergeist, and because of the risk of secondary injuries from hitting her head or her heart rate increasing, I shielded her with my body, repeatedly called her name, and tried to calm her down. My family called, and perhaps after hearing the sounds of the cat crying, screaming, and bumping into things, they finally understood how much she was suffering...

Even so, they said they could only stop the seizures, but I should bring her in if I wanted. ...They emphasized that any other treatment would have to wait until their regular morning hours, and I would have to go home.


However, I called two other hospitals, but they refused to help, saying they couldn't handle such a sudden situation, so I had no choice but to take him to Anihos.

From the beginning, I chose Anihos because they have nighttime services in case of emergencies, and the director himself told me to call anytime, but this is what actually happened.

He had small seizures on the examination table, and he might have been barely alive at that moment. He passed a large amount of blood in his urine, along with blood clots and kidney stones. I truly believe he endured and fought so hard without dying.

Anihos claimed there were no problems with the diagnosis or treatment, and the doctor who administered the IV, presumably, said on the phone, "We don't want any trouble, but he should be able to manage a seizure on his own." His condition was extremely critical, with organ rupture and cardiac arrest being very real possibilities. In any case, it's an unacceptable statement.

The hospital's tendency to conceal information is evident in their attempt to shift the blame for the seizures to a brain problem, trying to mislead the patient. They never provided a proper diagnosis until the very end, and we had to repeat the process of two urine samples and pain medication every day. Midway through my treatment, I was relieved to see a female doctor who seemed to understand my situation and was trying to adapt the treatment to my current condition. However, this was all a result of my repeated and strong communication about the abnormalities.

Furthermore, she declared that the seizures were a brain issue and therefore a more urgent problem. The fact that she was able to make a referral appointment at the University of Tokyo was a blessing in disguise, an unexpected relief.

Everything was different between Anihos and the University of Tokyo. The judgment, opinions, actions, prescriptions, and even how they interpreted ultrasounds were on completely different levels. Several kidney stones were visible at the University of Tokyo, but not at Anihos. I wanted to ask, "Will they disappear?" but they won't, right?

The hospital director was very busy and only returned from a business trip just before my University of Tokyo appointment. His name came up as a candidate, and I requested him, finally allowing me to see him. However, I still had many questions about his examination. On my last visit to Anihos the day before my University of Tokyo appointment, he said he didn't know if there were hidden kidney stones in other organs or not...??


The next day at the University of Tokyo, they confirmed that there were indeed kidney stones in various locations, and I saw it myself.

Also, while the medication to widen the ureters is apparently not rare at all, but rather a common drug, it was never prescribed at Aniphos. What was the point of all those morning and evening urine collections? I wish I could have given it to him sooner. He endured so much, having a catheter inserted into his injured and swollen urethra over and over again.

From the day after his visit to the University of Tokyo, daily urine collection was no longer necessary. Of course, time has passed, but everything is different.

The doctor at the University of Tokyo never mentioned anything about the brain. Hydronephrosis and urinary tract obstruction were the problems. The seizure was only that day, and even now, eight months later, he hasn't had a single seizure.

While it's a large hospital with excellent facilities, the young doctor seemed inexperienced, his judgment was poor, and he lacked adaptability; he was full of preconceived notions. Perhaps the hospital director is busy, but I think the guidance, education, and coordination are inadequate.

On my first visit for kidney stones, the hospital director examined me and told me that kidney stones can be fatal, and that he would keep me contactable at all times, even in the middle of the night, so I should call immediately if anything happened. But what's the reality?

I deeply regret this. To ensure this never happens again, we must carefully consider the patient's words rather than relying solely on textbooks. Assumptions are strictly forbidden; they can escalate into negligence, medical errors, and malpractice.

Did he really think that pouring water on my urethra would solve the problem when I said it was blocked and he still felt something was wrong?

Any doctor capable of imagining what's happening should have understood how dangerous it was.

Even with a water pipe, bursting is a possibility. The small leaks weren't normal or harmless; they were a leak before a burst. It's terrifying for a living organism.

Couldn't the hematuria also indicate uremia at that point?

And the seizures were a brain problem, which is more serious???


The day before my appointment at the University of Tokyo Hospital, the hospital director examined me and said that while no kidney stones were visible, my renal pelvis was dilated, whereas the ultrasound the previous day hadn't shown any dilation. At this timing???

The next day was already the University of Tokyo appointment. I had run out of energy to argue, so I just let it go, but weren't you disappointed that after all that resistance, they didn't press the issue...?

I've been worried many times about whether my condition had progressed beyond just kidney stones, and even after overcoming the worst of it, I kept asking various questions. Even with the bacterial infection, I reported the abnormality of the yellow pus, and that's how it was discovered through testing.

With the diagnosis and appropriate prescription from the University of Tokyo doctor, everything changed from the first day of my visit. I recovered remarkably quickly. I'm still doing well without any problems. I haven't had a single seizure.

By the way... at my first visit to Anihos, the head doctor explained that the therapeutic diet would have to be stopped after a few months. However, a professor at the University of Tokyo told me to continue the diet indefinitely. When I mentioned this, I was told that Urinary SO is formulated to be continued!

Considering this, I was relieved when they told me to call anytime on my first visit, but unfortunately, I now think there's a possibility that something was fundamentally wrong from the start.

These are my honest thoughts and observations based on the facts.
I haven't contacted them or visited them since the day before my appointment at the University of Tokyo, so I'm reporting and sharing this information here.

*On the third day after the initial consultation, I received a reply suggesting a visit to a university hospital, but instead, they insisted that I was fine and asked if I was already there. After that, my condition worsened, and on the day I nearly died from a seizure from midnight to early morning, they refused to admit me for an overnight stay, but they did admit me for that day only. When I picked up my child in the evening, they said they hadn't done anything except insert a catheter and bladder irrigation, and that they were too scared to give me an IV drip, even though I had wanted them to do it in parallel with the catheter insertion. They explained that I hadn't taken in any water or food, which made me feel extremely uneasy and angry. Then they started to shift the blame for the seizures to a brain problem, and the doctor on duty ran away. Finally, they said they couldn't see me at Aniphos, and that an MRI of my child's head was the priority, saying it was an emergency, and they started talking about making an appointment at the University of Tokyo. I knew that the seizures were not epilepsy or anything like that, so I made the appointment for a second opinion. What I told them on the phone was also true; it's not something that could be lied about. So, there's no point in arguing about it here. Eight months have passed since that intuition, and it has now been confirmed by facts. I have recorded it as a report and a warning, and in response to replies, I have made further facts public.

We're so grateful for the care of our three unique dogs at this vet clinic 🏥

From the attending veterinarian to the nurses and reception staff, everyone is incredibly kind and attentive!

Also, because they have a team of staff, even when the attending veterinarian isn't there, they understand the situation and we feel completely at ease bringing our dogs in.

Now that our dogs are seniors and have chronic illnesses, we visit the vet 2-3 times a week, which means we see the team of doctors and the nurses we've become familiar with much more often.

When we pass by the back of the examination room during a checkup, they always stop to say "You're doing so well today, you're amazing!" or call out "Ryo-kun" by name, and their kindness always makes us so happy ☺️

We'll be relying on their care for our three dogs for many more years to come, so we look forward to your continued support 🐶🐶🐶

Many hospitals refused to treat my case, but only Anihos allowed me to receive treatment.

I can't thank them enough. Thank you so much.

Even when I called back in an emergency, they remembered my name and said, "It's the one from earlier..." and treated my cat with all their might, even though she was in a truly critical condition. Sadly, my beloved cat crossed the Rainbow Bridge after only five days, but I am grateful to the attending veterinarian, the other doctors, nurses, reception staff, and everyone else involved.

Actually, my family's dog also received care here. Thanks to everyone, my dog ​​recovered enough to walk again, but due to her age, she crossed the Rainbow Bridge.

But both my cat and dog were waiting for my arrival.

Until then, they were desperately talking to them, encouraging them to hang in there until I arrived, and as a pet owner, I am incredibly grateful.

After what happened with my cat, we're thinking it would be a good idea to get our other cat checked out as well.

We'll be in touch again then!

The doctor is very caring and attentive.

The well-established medical system provides a sense of security. While appointments are available, there are fees involved, and you can't request a specific doctor. The high cost is a financial burden, but since nothing is more important than a life, I'm glad I was able to receive treatment at Anihos.

We always take care of our cats and dogs here.

We've been coming here for four years now.

The doctors and reception staff are all very kind, and we feel at ease every time we come.

They handle various surgeries, including spaying and neutering, and have a well-established management system. We feel it's a very trustworthy animal hospital.

The clinic is clean, and there's a sense of security that comes with a large hospital.
A parking attendant will guide you.

This is Pet Clinic Anihos.

We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience caused by the limited number of parking spaces.

Due to our location, we are unable to increase the number of spaces. However, if our parking lot is full, please use a nearby parking lot and bring your receipt; we will refund the full amount. Please rest assured that you can provide the receipt at a later date.
I can entrust my precious family to them with peace of mind, and I especially trust Dr. Suzuki.

Unlike local veterinarians, this clinic has excellent equipment, including clear ultrasounds and X-rays, so you can feel confident when dealing with complex illnesses or injuries.

The waiting room is clean and has a welcoming atmosphere. There's also parking available for several cars.
This is a great animal hospital.

They saved Lili-chan when she was on the verge of death.
They were so kind and gentle to our whole family, who were in tears,
and they performed the surgery,
and now she's a healthy senior dog.

I'm glad I came here, and I'm grateful to have found this hospital.
I'll continue to come here,
and I appreciate your continued support.

I've been using their services for about two years.
At the local veterinary clinic, they took blood tests and X-rays every day but couldn't figure out the cause of his symptoms, so I took him here and they quickly found the cause.
Also, the other day my pet accidentally ate some plastic, so when I called them in the middle of the night, they explained everything to me in detail and I felt really at ease.
All the doctors have excellent knowledge and skills, so I can visit them with peace of mind every time.

I've been going there for nearly 30 years.
All the doctors are highly motivated and work hard every day to support the animals and think of the best possible solutions.
They treat animals as a team, so there are several doctors who are aware of their condition, so I can visit at any time with peace of mind, even if the doctor in charge is not there.
The facilities are clean and I feel hospitality from everyone, from the receptionists to the nurses.
They are open 365 days a year and offer night-time consultations, so it's a hospital that makes me really glad I live so close to Anihos.

While there are some kind doctors, I lost my beloved cat due to medical malpractice at this hospital. The doctor who was treating my cat at the time apologized, but there was no apology from the doctor who harmed my cat. Afterwards, there were no letters or flowers either. I think you should avoid this hospital.

I was starting to feel increasingly uneasy with the hospital I had been going to, so I went to AniHos, a place I had been interested in for a while, and had Dr. Kuretake examine me, including for second consultations, and immediately made him my regular doctor. 

He's always so thorough with his examinations and explanations, and he listens carefully to my questions and even the smallest concerns, answering them sincerely, which I'm truly grateful for. 

Not only the doctors, but everyone at the hospital, from the receptionists to the nurses, is always so kind and polite. 

To this day, I've never had a bad experience asking a question or making a phone call; in fact, I'm always impressed by their wonderful service. 

Maybe it's because of the great atmosphere, but my child was fast asleep in the waiting room during his first appointment. lol

It's rare to find a hospital as good as this, so I highly recommend it to anyone who lives close enough to go!!!

I called the night-time emergency service about 100 times, but no one answered. I wanted to ask if there was a tick on my pet and if so, whether it would be best to have it removed at the emergency room, but I trusted them, so it's disappointing.
If you're busy with other dogs and cats, I would like someone else to keep your emergency phone. I have multiple pets, so if it was a tick, I wanted to do something about it before it spread to other pets.

I've been using this clinic for about 3-4 years. They're open at night, so I'm grateful that they can respond quickly in emergencies. 
Also, it used to be very busy, but since they started accepting appointments, waiting times have gotten shorter.

I've been a patient here several times, but the billing process is incredibly slow.

The other day, the examination finished relatively quickly, but even though it wasn't particularly busy, I waited an hour just to pay. It's infuriating that the administrative staff don't seem to think there's anything wrong with it.

The administrative staff are incredibly incompetent, and I hope they'll improve their service.
Every veterinarian will provide you with a thorough examination.

My cat was diagnosed with diabetes here. During the third visit, I was told that the hospital had made a mistake entering the amount during the first visit's billing process, and I was asked to pay an additional ¥11,800.

Furthermore, the blood glucose monitor (which was supposed to last two weeks) fitted during the third visit stopped working after only three days. Therefore, during the fourth visit, it was fitted again, but the doctor said that "free replacement is only available if it stops working on the day of fitting," so I paid ¥13,000 for a new device. However, that device also stopped working within a week.

Therefore, during the fifth visit, I paid another ¥13,000 for a new one fitted. However, despite being fitted at 4:30 PM that day, it was already unusable by 7:30 PM. When I called the hospital to request another fitting, the doctor said, "We currently have no stock, so we will contact you by phone."

Cats are extremely sensitive to changes in their environment. Having to take my pet to the vet so many times in such a short period of time due to these kinds of problems is truly heartbreaking and makes me feel incredibly sorry as a pet owner.

Furthermore, I have questions regarding the cost. The insulin I purchased at this vet cost ¥9,900 per vial, but the same product was around ¥3,700 at another vet. Even though veterinary fees are already not cheap, it's even more difficult to understand why this keeps happening.

Because it's a large hospital, I had a reassuring impression of it, which made it easy to schedule an initial consultation.

I haven't experienced any serious illnesses yet, so I mainly used it for health checkups. Since there are many veterinarians, I felt it was a hospital where I could find a suitable doctor and receive reassuring, consistent care, and prepare for my pet's future health.

There was one doctor I had an unpleasant experience with, so I told the receptionist I wanted to see a different doctor next time, and they accommodated my request, which was very helpful!

Of course, there were also many pleasant doctors, and they could perform diagnoses that other smaller hospitals couldn't, so I relied on them when my pet seemed unwell.

They provide a treatment plan and provide proper IC. The owner has the right to choose the treatment. They don't perform unnecessary tests, and my trust in them since I hospitalized my pet six years ago hasn't changed. If anything happens, I'll go to Anihos again.
Thank you for your help.

This is Pet Clinic Anihos. Thank you so much for your wonderful review and comments.

We are very pleased to hear that you found the veterinarian's explanations to be thorough. Thank you also for your kind words about our waiting room.

We will continue to strive to provide careful examinations and genuine care to pet owners and patients.
Thank you very much for your help.
From the reception staff to the doctors, everyone was incredibly kind and attentive. …
There were many teachers, so I was able to leave my child there with peace of mind.

This is a large animal hospital in the Jōhoku area. It has a parking lot, so it gets crowded. There are 7 spaces, plus one space for kei cars (mini cars). Bicycle parking is located further back. You can register from 7:30 in the morning, …

After a thorough examination, it was determined that I had a fracture and that surgery was necessary immediately. I was able to get an appointment at a university hospital, and everything turned out alright. If I had continued to wait and …
